notes.summary: Full-boundary domain, explicit R_red/top-degree conventions, zero anchor and exactly delimited qualified imports.
notes.detailedSummary: Only entire G331/B341 are granted; new geometry and energy are not imported. Every support is retained, with n-1 product slots and raw degree-n energy; lower-dimensional components remain but contribute zero. n0 is separate.
notes.text:
Domain, imports, and the theorem's conventions
Supports: G331, B341.

This is a mathematical draft, not an acceptance or a formal certificate. Only the ENTIRE qualified G331 and B341 are imported results. Their unchanged full bodies, mandatory annotations, ledgers, exact scopes and the SH17.4.7 colon qualification accompany this paper verbatim. The supplied ROOT342 and ROOT344 are unreviewed data: the new arguments below are not conditional on accepting either draft. No private active campaign was accessed.

Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be excellent local. **Throughout replace $R$ by $R_{\mathrm{red}}$, explicitly**, and use the image of each gauge there. This is a theory of its reduced semivaluation boundary, not a reconstruction of unreduced generic lengths. Put $n=\dim R$. When $n>0$, fix a proper $\mathfrak m$-primary ideal $\mathfrak a$ and the compact Hausdorff section
$$X_{\mathfrak a}=\{v:v(\mathfrak a)=1,\ 0<v(\mathfrak m)<\infty\}.$$
All prime supports strictly below $\mathfrak m$ are included. Functions are homogeneous of degree one on the centred rays. G331 supplies actual evaluation of exceptional Cartier divisors using the valued field of the support quotient, and supplies the independent geometric cone: actual negative effective finite real Cartier presentations, curve-nef on actual primary blowups. It proves its continuous uniform class $C$ equals the ideal uniform class, and its actual decreasing-net completion $D$ equals the geometric completion. We use its addition, nonnegative scaling (with $0u=0$), finite maxima, upper semicontinuity, primary-gauge cocycle, rational primary-or-unit profile density, full normalization-fibre descent, and density of the rational difference lattice of ideal gauges in $C(X_{\mathfrak a},\mathbb R)$. No arbitrary infimum or increasing-limit closure is imported.

B341 supplies **only** the bounded algebraic moment measures with $p=n-1$ potential slots, full all-field mixed kernel, symmetry/product/power/integral-closure laws, scalar ideal-moment order, real uniform continuity, bounded specified-limit decreasing-net continuity, one-factor gauge and top-degree residue-weighted normalization. It supplies actual curve zero-arity Cartier geometry and the bounded BFJ comparison in its precise published range. It supplies no higher-dimensional geometric comparison, locality, energy, or arbitrary finite-map theorem; n2--n3 provide the new geometric work.

Use raw degree-$n$ length coefficients, without dividing by $e_R(\mathfrak a)$. In a nonpure ring all smaller-dimensional components and all their supports remain in $X$ and $D$, but have zero contribution to this top-degree convention. Their own lower-arity energies would define additional conditions; they are not silently added. Put $m_{\mathfrak a}=e_R(\mathfrak a)>0$ and $\delta_{\mathfrak a}=m_{\mathfrak a}^{1/n}$. The additive energy anchor is the zero homogeneous potential. The constant $-1$ on this section is the homogeneous profile $-v(\mathfrak a)$; its reference mixed measure has raw mass $m_{\mathfrak a}$. A different gauge changes that homogeneous reference profile; it does not change the anchor zero.

The theorem constructed below is: a canonical energy $E:D\to[-\infty,0]$, its cone $E^1=\{E> -\infty\}$, finite positive Radon mixed measures on $(E^1)^{n-1}$, actual Cartier comparison on geometric cores, ordinary open locality, mixed integrability and polynomial variation, and continuity for every decreasing net with a specified $D$ and $E^1$ limit. Energy is invariant under primary changes, measures have exactly one gauge factor, and normalization/conductor descent uses every fibre and actual residue degrees. The smooth specialization is precisely the **finite-self-intersection extension of BFJ Definition 4.3**, proved in n8, rather than an assertion about a differently defined analytic or projective energy space. For $n=1$ this is actual reduced-curve linear Cartier energy. For $n=0$ set $E=0$ on the unique empty function and use the zero measure; no negative arity or division by $n$ is made.

notes.summary: Independent supported Cartier intersection: Artinian Euler polynomial, Koszul symmetry, actual divisor-cycle projection and raw Rees polarization.
notes.detailedSummary: Proof uses actual exceptional Cartier divisors on primary models, including nonnormal/non-CM/mixed-characteristic cases. Field-scheme Stacks intersection is applied only after an Artinian filtration; supported degree preserves DVR degree rather than global Chow degree.
notes.text:
Independent supported Cartier intersection
Supports: G331, B341, n1.

Write $Y=\operatorname{Bl}_I R$ for an actual primary blowup. It is reduced, projective, is the identity away from $\mathfrak m$, and every component dominates its reduced component of $R$. Its effective exceptional Cartier divisor $E_I$ has $\mathcal O_Y(-E_I)=\mathcal O_Y(1)$ ample. These facts follow also from whole Stacks31.33: its charts are $R[I/f]\subset R_f$, and $f$ is regular on its chart. Common product-ideal blowups dominate any finite collection. No arbitrary proper-model cofinality is needed.

For an effective exceptional integral Cartier divisor $E$, a power of $\mathfrak m$ kills $\mathcal O_E$: coherence and a finite affine cover give a common power from closed-fibre support. Its coherent cohomology has finite $R$-length by Stacks30.16. Define
$$\chi_R(E,\mathcal F)=\sum_j(-1)^j\ell_R H^j(E,\mathcal F).$$
For line bundles $L_i$ on $Y$, the function $\chi_R(E,\mathcal O_E\otimes\bigotimes_i L_i^{t_i})$ is a polynomial of total degree at most $p=n-1$. To prove this in mixed characteristic, filter $\mathcal O_E$ by the finitely many powers of $\mathfrak m$. Each successive coherent quotient lives on the proper residue-field scheme defined by $\mathfrak m\mathcal O_E$. Tensoring by a line bundle is exact; Euler additivity and Stacks33.45.1 give a finite sum of field-scheme polynomials. Supports have dimension at most $p$: on each integral component an exceptional regular equation cuts a divisor, and the excellent catenary dimension formula identifies its fibre dimension. No coefficient field is chosen and no nilpotent thickness is discarded.

For integral exceptional $F_1,\ldots,F_p$, define $Q_Y(F_1,\ldots,F_p,E)$ as the coefficient of $t_1\cdots t_p$ in this polynomial with $L_i=\mathcal O(F_i)$. For $p=0$ it is the finite zero-dimensional length. If $Z$ runs over integral reduced dimension-$p$ components of $E$, Stacks33.45.2, applied to each filtration quotient, gives
$$Q_Y(F_1,\ldots,F_p,E)=\sum_Z\ell_{\mathcal O_{Y,\eta_Z}}(\mathcal O_{E,\eta_Z})(\mathcal O(F_1)|_Z\cdots\mathcal O(F_p)|_Z\cdot Z).\tag{1}$$
Indeed localized composition lengths of the filtration add to the indicated length; the residue fields of the thickened and reduced local schemes are the same. Lower-dimensional supports give smaller polynomial degree. A fixed extra line-bundle twist cannot change the leading coefficient, since it shifts a polynomial's arguments by constants.

Polynomial substitution proves additivity in the first slots and their symmetry. The exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{E_1}(-E_2)\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{E_1+E_2}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{E_2}\longrightarrow0$$
and fixed-twist invariance prove additivity in the effective last slot. Every exceptional integral $F$ is a difference of effective ones, by G331's actual Cartier order unit $E_I$. This extends the last slot independently of decomposition, and then all slots extend to finite real presentations.

Full symmetry requires an actual supported calculation. For effective $E,F$, their two-term locally free Cartier complexes $[\mathcal O(-E)\to\mathcal O]$ and $[\mathcal O(-F)\to\mathcal O]$ have isomorphic tensor total complexes after signed interchange. Their cohomology is supported on $E\cap F$, hence over an Artinian base and of finite cohomological length. Computing its Euler characteristic in the two orders, with any invertible $L$, proves
$$\chi_R(E,L|_E)-\chi_R(E,L(-F)|_E)=\chi_R(F,L|_F)-\chi_R(F,L(-E)|_F).\tag{2}$$
This uses the locally free resolution of each Cartier divisor and Euler additivity; it does not require one divisor to be regular on the other. Take $L=\mathcal O(F)^t\mathcal O(E)^s\bigotimes_{j=1}^{n-2}\mathcal O(G_j)^{r_j}$. Set $t=s=0$ after taking the difference, and extract $r_1\cdots r_{n-2}$. The degree bound $n-1$ leaves only $t r_1\cdots r_{n-2}$ on the left, respectively $s r_1\cdots r_{n-2}$ on the right; higher powers cannot contribute. This exchanges $F$ and $E$. Effective differences and real linearity prove full $n$-slot symmetry. For $n=1$ no exchange is necessary.

Here is the precise projection argument. For $\operatorname{Spec}R$ use the dimension function $\delta(\mathfrak q)=\dim R/\mathfrak q$; catenarity in a local ring makes its drop across an immediate specialization exactly one, also for nonpure $R$. Extend by residue transcendence degree to finite-type models. Excellence supplies universal catenarity, so Stacks Situation42.7.1 and Lemma42.26.3 apply. For a proper map between primary models, or their finite normalization, corresponding top integral components map birationally, with function-field degree one. At a generic dimension-$p$ divisor point the local ring is reduced one-dimensional. Its injection into the finite sum of its minimal-component domain quotients has finite-length cokernel. For multiplication by a regular local Cartier equation, the cokernel's multiplication kernel and quotient have equal length. Consequently the Cartier divisor cycle is the sum of its component divisor cycles, with the top component generic weights one. Stacks42.26.3 therefore yields the **actual cycle** identity
$$f_*[f^*E]_p=[E]_p.\tag{3}$$
Smaller-dimensional components cut only smaller-dimensional cycles. Stacks33.45.7 now applies to the proper residue-field schemes in (1); components with smaller-dimensional image have zero intersection against $p$ pulled-back bundles. Thus
$$Q_{Y'}(f^*F_1,\ldots,f^*F_n)=Q_Y(F_1,\ldots,F_n).\tag{4}$$
This is supported degree, not a degree on global $\mathrm{CH}_0(Y)$. For a DVR the principal divisor $(t)$ has supported degree one although its global Chow class is zero. Formula (3) preserves exactly that degree. Residue extensions, inseparable as well as separable, remain in the field-scheme numerical degrees.

For a primary $I$, apply whole Stacks30.14.3 to the standard Rees algebra $A=\bigoplus I^q$ and $M=A$. It gives, as actual submodules of global rational sections, $H^0(Y,\mathcal O_Y(-qE_I))=I^q$ for large $q$. Stacks30.16.1(4) gives higher-cohomology vanishing. The Cartier exact sequence consequently gives
$$\chi_R(E_I,\mathcal O_{E_I}(-(q-1)E_I))=\ell_R(I^{q-1}/I^q).$$
Their degree-$p$ leading coefficients are $Q_Y((-E_I)^{[p]},E_I)/p!$ and $e_R(I)/p!$. Hence $-Q_Y((-E_I)^{[n]})=e_R(I)$. On a common product blowup put $D_{I_j}=-E_{I_j}$. For positive integers $t_j$ the product ideal has divisor $\sum t_jD_{I_j}$, so diagonal comparison and (4) give an identity of degree-$n$ polynomials. B341's length polynomial shows that the coefficient of $t_1\cdots t_n$ in its multiplicity is $n!e_R(I_1,\ldots,I_n)$. The Cartier coefficient is $-n!Q_Y(D_{I_1},\ldots,D_{I_n})$. Therefore
$$-Q_Y(D_{I_1},\ldots,D_{I_n})=e_R(I_1,\ldots,I_n).\tag{5}$$
Units give the zero divisor and zero coefficient. No comparison of coefficients of an inequality was used; no CM or infinite-field hypothesis entered this geometric argument.

notes.summary: Independent nonnegative divisorial core measures, supplied refinement lemma, fixed-primary invertible-image bridge and full bounded ordinary open locality.
notes.detailedSummary: Uses one fixed Bl_(I c0), actual J_q image equality and finite-span real intersections. Atomic strict maximum follows from invertible subideal restriction; two compact-cover limits extend locality to bounded actual D. No Borel/plurifine locality is claimed.
notes.text:
Positive geometric core measure, exact bridge, and bounded locality
Supports: G331, B341, n1, n2.

Normalize a primary model $Y$ finitely to $N$, retaining every top normal component. For its exceptional integral prime divisors $Z$ of dimension $p$, set $b_Z=\operatorname{ord}_Z(\mathfrak a)>0$ and $v_Z=\operatorname{ord}_Z/b_Z$ on $R$, with that component's prime support. For actual negative effective real curve-nef core divisors $D_i$, **define geometrically first**
$$\mu_Y(D_1,\ldots,D_p)=\sum_Z b_Z(\mathcal O(D_1)|_Z\cdots\mathcal O(D_p)|_Z\cdot Z)\delta_{v_Z}.\tag{6}$$
For $p=0$ the parenthesis is the residue-field degree of the point. There are finitely many exceptional primes. The weights are nonnegative: the restricted bundles are curve-nef on the projective integral residue-field scheme $Z$. On the **original actual primary model $Y$**, G331's correctly qualified real-nef-plus-ample and finite-span rationalization produce negative rational ample $L_{i,j}\to D_i$ in Cartier coefficient space. Their finite normalization pullbacks are ample by Stacks29.38.7(2), since a finite map is affine and thus quasi-affine; restrictions to the closed $Z$ remain ample. Clear denominators and apply Stacks33.45.9. Polynomial continuity on this finite span yields nonnegative weights at the limit. Thus no new Keeler theorem on an ungranted model or nonnormal Weil substitute is assumed, and no ideal-moment positivity defines the weights.

An explicit refinement lemma is needed before testing on larger models. A proper birational map of normal top components carries the dimension-$p$ exceptional primes either to smaller-dimensional strata, whose pulled-back $p$-bundle intersection is zero by33.45.7, or to an exceptional prime $Z$. In the latter case localize the base at $\eta_Z$, a DVR. Apply (3) to a uniformizer on a neighbourhood: the sum of positive integer orders times residue degrees over $Z$ is one. Thus there is exactly one dominating prime, its order and residue degree are one, and its DVR valuation equals that of $Z$. To see the last assertion directly, both DVRs have the same fraction field and the second dominates the first. Writing every field element as a uniformizer power times a unit in the first forces identical orders. The numerical projection formula preserves its intersection weight and $b_Z$. Normalizations of common primary refinements map to $N$ by the normalization universal property, componentwise. Therefore (6) is unchanged as a measure on the full boundary under every primary refinement. This fills the refinement step before any algebraic identification.

For an exceptional Cartier test $F$ determined on the same model, $H_F(v_Z)=\operatorname{ord}_Z(F)/b_Z$. The normal divisor cycle and (1),(4) give
$$\int H_F\,d\mu_Y(D_1,\ldots,D_p)=Q_Y(D_1,\ldots,D_p,F).\tag{7}$$
For tests determined only on a common larger primary model, the refinement lemma reduces to this formula there.

We now prove the bridge for real cores, rather than infer intersection convergence from function convergence. On a fixed common $Y$, let $T=H^0(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$. G331 supplies a fixed $h$ with $\mathfrak m^h(T/R)=0$, and the **primary** $\mathfrak c_0=\mathfrak m^{h+1}$ satisfies $\mathfrak c_0T\subset\mathfrak m$ as elements of $R$. For a negative rational ample exceptional $L$, sufficiently divisible large $q$ makes $\mathcal O_Y(qL)$ globally generated. Put $J_q=\mathfrak c_0H^0(Y,\mathcal O_Y(qL))\subset R$. This is a proper ideal, unit off the closed point by localization of sections, hence primary. Fix **one** refinement $Y'=\operatorname{Bl}_{I\mathfrak c_0}R$, and let $D_0$ be the pulled-back negative divisor of $\mathfrak c_0$. Global generation is a surjection onto an actual invertible subideal of $\mathcal O_Y$. Right exact pullback, then multiplication by the invertible image of $\mathfrak c_0$, gives the actual image equality
$$J_q\mathcal O_{Y'}=\mathcal O_{Y'}(qf^*L+D_0).\tag{8}$$
The inclusion into $\mathcal O_{Y'}$ remains injective because its Cartier local equation is nonzero on every reduced generic component. Thus (8) is stronger than equality of valuations. The blowup universal property gives $Y'\to\operatorname{Bl}_{J_q}R$. For simultaneous $L_i,q_i$, (4),(5),(8) yield
$$\frac{e_R(J_{1,q_1},\ldots,J_{n,q_n})}{\prod q_i}=-Q_{Y'}(f^*L_1+D_0/q_1,\ldots,f^*L_n+D_0/q_n).\tag{9}$$
All intersections are on this one model. Evaluations satisfy $-v(J_q)/q=H_L-v(\mathfrak c_0)/q$, uniformly since $\mathfrak c_0$ is primary.

For every actual negative effective real nef $D_i$ on $Y$, G331's finite-span perturbation and upward rational rounding give negative rational ample $L_{i,j}\to D_i$ in coefficient space. Their evaluations converge uniformly. Use the same $\mathfrak c_0,Y'$ for all $i,j$, choosing divisible $q_{i,j}\to\infty$ with global generation. Equation (9) and polynomial intersection continuity converge to $-Q_Y(D_1,\ldots,D_n)$; the uniformly approximating profiles converge to $H_{D_i}$. B341's uniform moment continuity and continuous test pairing give the same limit on the algebraic side. Therefore the algebraic bounded form on core tuples is $-Q$, and its measure satisfies (7).

Every exceptional integral Cartier test $F$ is a difference of two negative ample exceptional divisors: choose $N$ so $F-NE_I$ is negative ample, and subtract $-NE_I$. Extend by real linearity and use common primary refinements. In particular every primary ideal test is covered. Dense ideal-difference tests and finite mass identify (6) with B341's measure on every core tuple. This proves actual geometric presentation and primary-model independence, not just algebraic presentation independence.

Here is strict maximum locality on rational cores. Synchronize denominators and write $u=-v(A)/q$, $w=-v(B)/q$. On a common normalized primary model make $A,B,A+B$ and the remaining ideals invertible. Divide their image ideals by $S=(A+B)\mathcal O_N$ to obtain actual invertible subideals $L=A\mathcal O_N/S$, $M=B\mathcal O_N/S$, with $L+M=\mathcal O_N$. At an atom $Z$ with $u(v_Z)>w(v_Z)$, $\operatorname{ord}_Z(M)>0$. The map $M|_Z\to\mathcal O_Z$ vanishes generically and therefore everywhere, since $Z$ is integral and this is a line-bundle morphism. Restricting $L+M=\mathcal O_N$ gives $L|_Z\simeq\mathcal O_Z$. Hence $D_A|_Z$ and $D_{A+B}|_Z$ have the same bundle class and intersection weight with every fixed other input. On this common atomic support
$$\mu(\max(u,w),u_2,\ldots,u_p)|_{\{u>w\}}=\mu(u,u_2,\ldots,u_p)|_{\{u>w\}}.\tag{10}$$
Unit/zero cases are included in the subideal argument. There is no regularity or SNC assumption on closed points of $N$.

Uniform rational approximation proves (10) for continuous $u,w$ and continuous other slots: a continuous test supported on compact $K\subset\{u>w\}$ has a uniform positive gap there; apply (10) to approximants and pass weakly to the limit. Actual bounded decreasing representations then extend the other slots to bounded $D$, keeping the open set fixed. Compact regularity and Urysohn functions supported inside an open set identify Radon restrictions.

We need uniform weak continuity on bounded $D$ as well. B341's scalar order and additive negative-constant expansion give, if entries are in $[-M,0]$ and coordinatewise distance at most $\varepsilon$,
$$|B_{\boldsymbol u}(v(J))-B_{\boldsymbol w}(v(J))|\le[(M+\varepsilon)^p-M^p]e_R(\mathfrak a^{[p]},J).\tag{11}$$
Both comparisons use $u_i-\varepsilon\le w_i$; expanding the shifts bounds every term with $r$ constant slots by $\varepsilon^r M^{p-r}e_R(\mathfrak a^{[p]},J)$. Dense tests and the common mass bound extend this to weak convergence. This asserts continuity inside the established domain, not increasing-limit membership.

Finally suppose bounded $u,w\in D$ agree on open $U$. Take actual decreasing $C$ representations $u_\alpha,w_\beta$, with common bound $[-M,0]$; their terms already dominate the targets, or may be clamped there. For compact $K\subset U$, fixed $\alpha$, and $\varepsilon>0$, the open sets $\{w_\beta-\varepsilon<u_\alpha\}$ cover $K$. Finite subcover and directedness give one $\beta_0$ whose open set contains $K$ and works for every later $\beta$. Continuous strict locality gives equality of the test integrals for $\max(u_\alpha,w_\beta-\varepsilon)$ and $u_\alpha$. First take the bounded decreasing $\beta$ limit, whose specified domain limit is $\max(u_\alpha,w-\varepsilon)$, then the $\alpha$ limit to $\max(u,w-\varepsilon)$. These are two justified limits, not a flattening assertion. Reverse the roles. The two maxima are within $\varepsilon$ uniformly of the already known $D$ function $\max(u,w)$. Equation (11) gives the common limit, proving equality of the measures on $U$. Replacing slots successively proves full bounded mixed ordinary open locality. The $p=0$ case is equality of the fixed reference measure.

notes.summary: Full bounded symmetric n-form with genuine discontinuous D pairing; arbitrary fixed-slot Cauchy, n-entry Holder, Minkowski and concavity.
notes.detailedSummary: Directed Radon supremum is proved for continuous families. All three multiplicities use the same simultaneous superficial 2D quotient; R(z) handles finite fields and no CM/deletion assumption is made. Finite integer simplex proves generalized Holder; printed SH colon is not used.
notes.text:
Bounded full form, directed integration, and the mixed inequalities
Supports: G331, B341, n1, n2, n3.

For rational primary-or-unit profiles $u_i=-v(I_i)/q_i$ define
$$F(u_1,\ldots,u_n)=e_R(I_1,\ldots,I_n)/(q_1\cdots q_n).\tag{12}$$
B341's kernel makes this independent of all presentations, symmetric, additive on the negative cone and nonnegative, with order reversed relative to the functions in **all $n$ slots**. For $u_i\in[-M,0]$, its bound is $M^n m_{\mathfrak a}$. Negative-constant shifts give the error bound $[(M+\varepsilon)^n-M^n]m_{\mathfrak a}$ for uniformly close rational tuples. Thus uniform approximation defines the same symmetric form on $C$, with all these identities for real scalars.

For bounded $D$ tuples choose actual decreasing $C$ representations in all $n$ entries. Their scalar forms increase, bounded as above. Their supremum is representation independent: for any fixed continuous majorant $h_i\ge u_i$, $\{g_{i,\alpha}<h_i+\varepsilon\}$ is a directed open cover; compactness selects a common eventual index in each of the finitely many slots. Then $g_{i,\alpha}-\varepsilon\le h_i$, so order and the shift error compare $F(\boldsymbol h)$ to the representation supremum. Reverse the two representations and let $\varepsilon\to0$. This also proves order for arbitrary bounded $D$ entries and
$$F(\boldsymbol u)=\sup\{F(\boldsymbol h):h_i\in C,\ h_i\ge u_i\}.\tag{13}$$
Addition and homogeneity use actual product-index $C$ representations of sums and scalar multiples; their finite scalar limits commute with finite sums. If bounded $D$ nets decrease to a specified bounded $D$ tuple with a common bound, their USC strict-test open covers compared to each fixed $C$ majorant prove convergence of the forms using the same error. No new membership of an infimum is asserted. For continuous $v\in C$, ideal approximation and B341's bounded weak continuity prove
$$F(v,u_1,\ldots,u_p)=\int(-v)\,d\mu(u_1,\ldots,u_p).\tag{14}$$

The following measure lemma justifies an actual discontinuous test. Let $f_\alpha$ be a directed increasing family of nonnegative continuous functions on compact Hausdorff $X$ and $f=\sup f_\alpha$, possibly infinite. For finite positive Radon $\sigma$,
$$\int f\,d\sigma=\sup_\alpha\int f_\alpha\,d\sigma.\tag{15}$$
Here is a proof including the regularity step. For any nonnegative continuous $h\le f$, the open sets $\{f_\alpha>h-\varepsilon\}$ cover $X$; directed compactness gives one index and thus $\int f_\alpha\ge\int h-\varepsilon\sigma(X)$. Also $\int f$ is the supremum of these continuous-minorant integrals: first truncate $f$ at a finite level and partition its range into finitely many steps. Each open superlevel set admits compact subsets whose measure approximates it from below. Urysohn functions equal to one on these compacts and supported inside the superlevel sets, multiplied by the step increments and summed, give a continuous nonnegative minorant with integral approximating the step integral. For increments of size $\eta$ and levels $j\eta$, the sum $\eta\sum_j h_j$ is at most $f$ pointwise, because nonzero $h_j$ requires $f>j\eta$; the approximation error is at most $\eta\sigma(X)$ plus the finitely many chosen compact errors. Let errors and step size vanish and then the truncation level grow. Ordinary sequence integration applies to the finite-level scalar approximations. This proves the assertion and (15). It is not monotone convergence for arbitrary measurable nets, which would be false.

If bounded $v\in D$ has an actual decreasing $C$ representation $g_\alpha$, apply (15) to $-g_\alpha\uparrow-v$ against the fixed measure in (14). For each fixed $g_\alpha$, (14) gives its integral. Commuting its supremum with the independent potential-representation suprema proves (14) for this discontinuous bounded $D$ test. Directly testing weak convergence by $v$ would not justify it.

We now prove conditional Cauchy for arbitrary fixed mixed entries. The fresh published input is the complete immediate proof of SH17.7.1, valid for every two-dimensional Noetherian local ring and finite two-dimensional module. Its argument is as follows. Pass to $R(z)$ if necessary, preserving dimension and all finite lengths by composition series. Choose a two-generated reduction $(a,b)$ of the primary ideal $I$. For positive integers $r,s,N$, the quotient length estimate
$$\ell(M/I^{rN}J^{sN}M)\le2\ell(M/J^{sN}M)+\ell(M/(a^{rN},b^{rN})M)$$
follows by replacing $I^{rN}$ by $(a^{rN},b^{rN})$ and mapping two copies of $M/J^{sN}M$ onto the remaining subquotient. Divide by $N^2/2$. Lech's parameter asymptotic formula and reduction invariance give
$$e(I^rJ^s;M)\le2e(I;M)r^2+2e(J;M)s^2.$$
The mixed polynomial expands its left side as $e(I)r^2+2e(I,J)rs+e(J)s^2$. Optimizing rational $r/s$ yields $e(I,J)^2\le e(I)e(J)$, since mixed multiplicity is nonnegative (and positive for primary slots). The complete SH17.7.2--3 statements/proofs were checked as context; the arbitrary fixed-slot result below is stronger than simply citing their two-ideal diagonal sequence.

For $n>2$ and proper $K_3,\ldots,K_n$, simultaneously choose one superficial element in $K_3$ for the three families $(K_3,\ldots,K_n,I,I)$, $(K_3,\ldots,K_n,I,J)$, $(K_3,\ldots,K_n,J,J)$. SH17.2.2's proof removes finitely many proper subspaces in the same $K_3/\mathfrak mK_3$, with minimal-prime avoidance included. Their intersection has a point over the infinite residue field. SH17.4.6 applies to each family on this same quotient, of dimension exactly $n-1$: minimal-prime avoidance gives the upper bound, and a lifted parameter system and the height theorem give the lower bound. Repeat in the fixed slots. This produces the **same two-dimensional quotient** for all three numbers; it can be nonreduced, non-CM and have embedded or smaller-dimensional components. Nothing is deleted, and no regular sequence is claimed. Apply the just-checked two-dimensional inequality there. In a finite residue field the exact extension $R(z)$ changes no length polynomial; it is only an algebraic device and no boundary equivalence is assumed. We obtain
$$F(x,y,K_3,\ldots,K_n)^2\le F(x,x,K_3,\ldots,K_n)F(y,y,K_3,\ldots,K_n).\tag{16}$$
The needed superficial/reduction foundations are SH17.2.1--4 and17.4.6, checked in full; SH17.4.7's literal unquotiented colon is not used. Its correction is the finite annihilator on the quotient by previous parameters. Ordinary reduction existence, power-reduction invariance and Lech's formula are disclosed earlier published dependencies; complete11.2.9--10 were additionally read, while every historical reduction proof is not claimed freshly reconstructed. Unit slots follow by adding $-\varepsilon v(\mathfrak a)$ and uniform continuity; real $C$ and bounded $D$ entries follow by their proved form limits. For $n=1$ the form is linear.

Here is generalized $n$-entry Holder, with the finite-simplex argument included. For finitely many proper ideal types consider counts $\alpha_i\ge0$, $\sum\alpha_i=n$, and subtract $\sum\alpha_i\log F(u_i^{[n]})/n$ from $\log F(u^{\boldsymbol\alpha})$. Call this $f(\alpha)$; primary positivity makes each logarithm finite and $f=0$ at the vertices. By (16), for positive $\alpha_i,\alpha_j$,
$$2f(\alpha)\le f(\alpha+e_i-e_j)+f(\alpha-e_i+e_j).$$
If its finite global maximum were positive, choose a maximizer with the smallest support. Both displayed neighbours must be maximizers. Repeatedly transfer one unit from $j$ to $i$ until $j$ vanishes; every intermediate point remains a maximizer by the same inequality. This contradicts minimal support. Consequently $f\le0$. Perturbing zero entries by $-\varepsilon$, then taking uniform and bounded decreasing limits, proves
$$F(u_1,\ldots,u_n)\le\prod_i A(u_i),\qquad A(u)=F(u^{[n]})^{1/n}.\tag{17}$$
Expanding $F((u+w)^{[n]})$ and applying (17) termwise gives $A(u+w)\le A(u)+A(w)$. For a signed cone difference $z=U-V$, (16) implies
$$F(z,z,K)=F(U,U,K)+F(V,V,K)-2F(U,V,K)\ge0.$$
Each direction in a cone segment is such a difference. Thus $E_{\mathrm{bd}}(u)=-F(u^{[n]})/n$ is concave: its second derivative is $-(n-1)F(z,z,u_t^{[n-2]})\le0$; for $n=1$ it is linear. No strictness or separation follows in nonpure rings.

notes.summary: Truncation E1 and full majorant supremum; noncircular approximation without common bound, cone closure, canonical measures and full decreasing E1 nets.
notes.detailedSummary: Finite target sizes provide uniform scalar shift errors before unbounded additivity. E1 cone closure is proved first; moments and density yield finite Radon measures. Decreasing-net continuity requires a specified D/E1 limit; no arbitrary-infimum or increasing closure is asserted.
notes.text:
Finite energy, noncircular approximation, and every decreasing net
Supports: G331, B341, n1, n3, n4.

For $u\in D$ put $u^k=\max(u,-k)\in D^{\mathrm{bd}}$, and define initially extended forms
$$F_\infty(u_1,\ldots,u_n)=\sup_{k_1,\ldots,k_n}F(u_1^{k_1},\ldots,u_n^{k_n}),\quad E(u)=-F_\infty(u^{[n]})/n,\quad E^1=\{u\in D:E(u)>-\infty\}.\tag{18}$$
Use positive integers for $k_i$; allowing real levels is cofinal. Scalar monotonicity makes these suprema well defined. The exact formula on the entire $D$ domain, also for infinite values, is
$$F_\infty(\boldsymbol u)=\sup\{F(\boldsymbol h):h_i\in C,\ h_i\ge u_i\}.\tag{19}$$
For one direction, a fixed finite continuous majorant $h_i$ dominates $u_i^{k_i}$ once $k_i\ge\|h_i\|$, so order gives $F(\boldsymbol h)\le F_\infty(\boldsymbol u)$. For the other direction (13) for each truncation uses only $C$ majorants that also majorize $u_i$. This proves both bounds without a finite lower bound on $u_i$ and without new completion membership.

Write $A_i=F_\infty(u_i^{[n]})^{1/n}$. Inequality (17) on truncations proves $F_\infty(\boldsymbol u)\le\prod A_i$ for $u_i\in E^1$. Every $D$ majorant of an $E^1$ function is in $E^1$ by truncation order, with no larger size. Globally bottom has infinite energy since $F((-k)^{[n]})=k^n m_{\mathfrak a}$. Poles confined to components invisible to top degree may have finite energy; they remain points of the domain.

Before unbounded additivity we prove a bounded approximation lemma. Suppose $f_{i,\lambda}\in D^{\mathrm{bd}}$ decrease to specified $u_i\in E^1$, each term individually bounded, with **no common finite lower bound required**. For a fixed $C$ majorant tuple $h_i\ge u_i$ and $\varepsilon>0$, USC gives open sets $\{f_{i,\lambda}<h_i+\varepsilon\}$ covering $X$. Directed compactness supplies one eventual index for all slots with $f_{i,\lambda}-\varepsilon\le h_i$. Each term has diagonal size at most $A_i$. Bounded additivity and (17) bound its shift error by
$$0\le F(f_{1,\lambda}-\varepsilon,\ldots,f_{n,\lambda}-\varepsilon)-F(\boldsymbol f_\lambda)\le\prod_i(A_i+\varepsilon\delta_{\mathfrak a})-\prod_i A_i.\tag{20}$$
The right side sums the nonempty subsets of shifted slots using Holder; it does not depend on the individual sup norms. Order compares the shifted tuple to $\boldsymbol h$. Let $\varepsilon\to0$ and then take the supremum (19). The increasing scalar limit is
$$F(\boldsymbol f_\lambda)\uparrow F_\infty(\boldsymbol u).\tag{21}$$
The upper bound follows also by extending each bounded term to its own truncation formula. Separate indices are handled by the actual finite product directed set. This proof uses no unbounded additivity.

To prove cone closure first, take $u,w\in E^1$ and $s_k=u^k+w^k\downarrow u+w\in D$. The last membership is G331's actual product-representation addition rule. Bounded Minkowski gives $A(s_k)\le A(u)+A(w)$. For any $h\in C$ majorizing $u+w$, the open sets $\{s_k<h+\varepsilon\}$ cover $X$, so one $k$ has $s_k-\varepsilon\le h$. Bounded Holder and Minkowski give $F(h^{[n]})\le(A(u)+A(w)+\varepsilon\delta_{\mathfrak a})^n$. Formula (19) and $\varepsilon\to0$ prove $u+w\in E^1$ and Minkowski there. Positive scaling follows from cofinal rescaled cutoff levels, and scalar zero is treated separately as the zero function. Now apply (21) to sums of truncations and to the other truncated entries. Bounded additivity passes to the finite limits. Thus $F_\infty$ is a finite symmetric additive cone $n$-form on $E^1$, nonnegative-real homogeneous, with order, (16),(17) and Minkowski. Concavity passes by bounded approximations, or by its finite polynomial on each segment.

For $u_1,\ldots,u_p\in E^1$, their bounded truncation measures have primary moments
$$\int v(J)\,d\mu(u_1^{k_1},\ldots,u_p^{k_p})=F(u_1^{k_1},\ldots,u_p^{k_p},-v(J)),$$
which increase to finite $F_\infty(u_1,\ldots,u_p,-v(J))$. Their masses are at most $\delta_{\mathfrak a}\prod_{i=1}^p A_i$. Difference-lattice test integrals therefore converge and remain positive on nonnegative tests. Their uniform mass bound extends the limit to a unique positive continuous functional on $C(X)$, hence a finite positive Radon measure, denoted $\mu_E(\boldsymbol u)$. Explicitly approximate any continuous test uniformly by a rational difference-lattice test and bound both integral errors by its sup-norm error times the common mass bound. This proves actual weak convergence of the net, without a compactness subsequence or metrizability assertion. Its exact moment rule is
$$\int v(J)\,d\mu_E(\boldsymbol u)=F_\infty(\boldsymbol u,-v(J)).\tag{22}$$
Lemma (21) proves the same convergence for **any individually bounded decreasing $D$ approximants** to the specified finite-energy targets. Thus the construction is canonical, agrees with B341 on bounded inputs, and inherits additivity/homogeneity by moments and density. It is geometrically compared on cores by n3.

For an arbitrary decreasing net $u_{i,\lambda}\in E^1$ with specified $u_i\in E^1$ limit in $D$, all sizes are at most $A_i$. USC compact covers compare them to every fixed $C$ majorant tuple as above. Now the already proved unbounded multilinearity and Holder give (20) for $F_\infty$. Taking $\varepsilon\to0$ and supremum (19) proves
$$F_\infty(\boldsymbol u_\lambda)\uparrow F_\infty(\boldsymbol u).\tag{23}$$
Fixed primary tests give every measure moment; the same common mass bound proves weak convergence $\mu_E(\boldsymbol u_\lambda)\to\mu_E(\boldsymbol u)$. Diagonals give $E(u_\lambda)\downarrow E(u)$. This is a theorem for full directed nets, not just sequences. It does not assert membership of arbitrary infima. One useful extra follows without circularity: if a decreasing $E^1$ net has a **specified $D$ limit** and uniformly bounded sizes, compact-cover comparison to each majorant and (19) prove that limit belongs to $E^1$; then (23) applies. Specified $D$ membership remains essential.

notes.summary: Extended D test pairing, E1 integrability, polynomial variation, finite reference cocycle, elementary capacity estimate and finite-energy open locality.
notes.detailedSummary: Actual C representations and justified suprema prove E1 pairing; truncations give extended D pairing. Capacity estimate proves E1 pole capacity zero but no Choquet/quasicontinuity or strict nonpluripolar cutoff theorem. Concavity has no uniqueness implication.
notes.text:
Unbounded pairing, variations, capacity, and ordinary locality
Supports: G331, B341, n1, n3, n4, n5.

For $v\in E^1$, take an actual decreasing $C$ representation $g_\alpha\downarrow v$. Each $g_\alpha$ is bounded and majorizes $v$, so its size is at most $A(v)$. Equation (15) against the **fixed** finite-energy measure gives
$$\int(-v)\,d\mu_E(\boldsymbol u)=\sup_\alpha\int(-g_\alpha)\,d\mu_E(\boldsymbol u).$$
For fixed $g_\alpha$, continuous-test weak convergence in n5 identifies its integral with $\sup_{\boldsymbol k}F(g_\alpha,\boldsymbol u^{\boldsymbol k})$. These nonnegative scalar suprema commute. Lemma (21) applies to the product net $(g_\alpha,\boldsymbol u^{\boldsymbol k})$ of individually bounded functions with finite-energy targets. Hence
$$\int(-v)\,d\mu_E(u_1,\ldots,u_p)=F_\infty(v,u_1,\ldots,u_p)\le A(v)\prod_iA(u_i)<\infty.\tag{24}$$
This supplies actual integrability for discontinuous or unbounded tests. It does not use weak convergence against such a test. Every such mixed measure gives zero mass to the pole set of **every** $v\in E^1$, since otherwise (24) would be infinite. In particular
$$E(u)=\frac1n\int u\,d\mu_E(u^{[p]}).\tag{25}$$

There is also the fully extended test identity for every $v\in D$, with the other entries in $E^1$: its bounded truncations $v^k$ are in $E^1$, so (24) applies to each. Ordinary nonnegative sequence integration gives $\int(-v)=\sup_k\int(-v^k)$. By the defining cutoff formula (18), the suprema over $k$ and the other entries' cutoffs commute and are cofinal in the complete product cutoff set. Hence $\int(-v)\,d\mu_E(\boldsymbol u)=F_\infty(v,\boldsymbol u)$ in $[0,\infty]$. Finiteness and no pole mass are asserted only when the test is $E^1$ (or its displayed mixed value happens to be finite).

For $u,v\in E^1$, finite polynomial multilinearity gives, for $t\ge0$,
$$\frac{d}{dt}E(u+tv)=-F_\infty(v,(u+tv)^{[p]})=\int v\,d\mu_E((u+tv)^{[p]}).\tag{26}$$
At zero this is a one-sided derivative. On an admissible segment with direction $v-u$, cone differences give the same polynomial derivative, with absolute integrability by (24) applied to each term. Its second derivative is nonpositive by (16), so $E$ is concave on the whole finite-energy cone. No variation outside the class is asserted.

For a fixed finite-energy reference $w$, define $E_w(u)=E(u)-E(w)$. Telescoping the $n$-form gives the full finite reference-cocycle formula
$$E_w(u)=\frac1n\sum_{j=0}^{p}\int(u-w)\,d\mu_E(u^{[j]},w^{[p-j]}).\tag{27}$$
Each term is absolutely integrable by (24) separately for $u,w$. Consequently $E_w(u)+E_z(w)=E_z(u)$. In particular $E_0=E$, $E(0)=0$, $E(-1)=-m_{\mathfrak a}/n$, and $\mu_E((-1)^{[p]})(X)=m_{\mathfrak a}$; zero entries annihilate positive-arity measures and forms as dictated by multilinearity. The $n=1$ operator has no potential entries, so that annihilation statement has no zero-arity analogue.

For Borel $A$ define the elementary capacity
$$\operatorname{Cap}_{\mathfrak a}(A)=\sup\{\mu(\phi^{[p]})(A):\phi\in D^{\mathrm{bd}},\ -1\le\phi\le0\}.$$
It is monotone and countably subadditive by the same properties for each measure and $\sup_\phi\sum_j\le\sum_j\sup_\phi$. Its total value is at most $m_{\mathfrak a}$. For $u\in E^1$, $t>0$, (24) and $A(\phi)\le\delta_{\mathfrak a}$ give
$$\operatorname{Cap}_{\mathfrak a}(\{u<-t\})\le A(u)\delta_{\mathfrak a}^{p}/t.\tag{28}$$
Thus every $E^1$ pole set has this capacity zero. This estimate alone is not a Choquet theorem or a quasicontinuity theorem. No capacity regularity, equation uniqueness, or measure order is inferred from scalar moment order.

If two finite-energy tuples agree entrywise on an open $U$, their corresponding constant truncations agree there. N3 gives equality of their bounded mixed restrictions. A continuous test supported on compact $K\subset U$ passes to the finite-energy weak limit of n5. Urysohn functions and Radon regularity determine restrictions, proving ordinary open locality for $\mu_E$. We do not assert a nonpluripolar cutoff identity on $\{u>-k\}$: for upper semicontinuous $u$ that strict Borel set need not be open, and neither the proved locality nor the capacity estimate establishes such an identity. The constructed calculus uses bounded decreasing extension; it makes no claim to an unproved Borel/plurifine extension convention.

notes.summary: Gauge energy invariance with exactly one measure factor; inseparable residue-weighted normalization, full fibre-constant E1 descent, actual curves and empty case.
notes.detailedSummary: Variable cuts max(u,-k v_a(b)) are squeezed by constant cuts. Only top-dimensional normalization centres enter raw degree-n energy, while all lower-dimensional supports remain in conductor compatibility. R_red is explicit; arbitrary finite-map operator traces are not claimed.
notes.text:
Primary energy invariance, full conductor descent, and dimensions one and zero
Supports: G331, B341, n1, n4, n5, n6.

For another proper primary $\mathfrak b$, put $d(v)=v_{\mathfrak a}(\mathfrak b)$ and $T(v)=v/d(v)$. On compact $X_{\mathfrak a}$, $0<d_{\min}\le d\le d_{\max}<\infty$, and $u_{\mathfrak b}(Tv)=u_{\mathfrak a}(v)/d(v)$. G331 transports actual $C,D$ representations. B341 gives for every bounded tuple
$$\mu_{\mathfrak b}(\boldsymbol u_{\mathfrak b})=T_*[d\,\mu_{\mathfrak a}(\boldsymbol u_{\mathfrak a})].\tag{29}$$
Use the actual bounded-test pairing of n4, including discontinuous inputs, to cancel $d$ against the last transformed potential. This proves invariance of the full bounded $n$-form, not just ideal moments.

For an unbounded $u$, pulling its $\mathfrak b$-truncation back with its homogeneous factor gives $w_k=\max(u_{\mathfrak a},-kd)$. It is bounded $D$ by finite maxima with the primary profile $-k v_{\mathfrak a}(\mathfrak b)$, and
$$\max(u_{\mathfrak a},-k d_{\max})\le w_k\le\max(u_{\mathfrak a},-k d_{\min}).\tag{30}$$
The two constant cutoff levels are cofinal. Bounded form invariance and scalar order therefore prove $F_{\infty,\mathfrak b}(u_{\mathfrak b}^{[n]})=F_{\infty,\mathfrak a}(u_{\mathfrak a}^{[n]})$, including infinite values. Thus $E^1$ is primary-gauge independent. For an $E^1$ tuple, $(w_{i,k})$ are individually bounded decreasing approximants to the original tuple. Apply (21),(22) and test the weak limits in (29) with the fixed continuous function $d$ times a transported continuous test. We obtain
$$F_{\infty,\mathfrak b}(\boldsymbol u_{\mathfrak b})=F_{\infty,\mathfrak a}(\boldsymbol u_{\mathfrak a}),\quad E_{\mathfrak b}(u_{\mathfrak b})=E_{\mathfrak a}(u_{\mathfrak a}),\quad\mu_{E,\mathfrak b}=T_*[d\,\mu_{E,\mathfrak a}].\tag{31}$$
There is exactly **one** measure factor, not $d^n$, $d^{n-1}$ or an inverse factor. For $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak a^r$, it is $r$, while potentials divide by $r$. G331's homogeneous cocycle makes (31) compose exactly for three primary gauges. A finite reference $w$ is transported along with $u$, so (27) and its cocycle are invariant as well.

Let $S$ normalize $R$ finitely, with all local normal centres $S_q$ over $\mathfrak m$. Write $f_q=[\kappa(q):\kappa(\mathfrak m)]$ and $\rho_q$ for the full restriction map of their sections with gauge $\mathfrak aS_q$. These are total residue degrees, including inseparable ones. B341's bounded top-degree identity, paired with a bounded $D$ test using n4, gives the full bounded $n$-form identity. For an extended $D$ tuple, constant truncations pull back exactly to constant truncations on every centre. There are finitely many centres and all forms are nonnegative; finite sums commute with increasing scalar suprema. Therefore, with extended values allowed,
$$F_{\infty,R}(\boldsymbol u)=\sum_{\dim S_q=n}f_q F_{\infty,S_q}(\rho_q^*\boldsymbol u),\qquad E_R(u)=\sum_{\dim S_q=n}f_q E_{S_q}(\rho_q^*u).\tag{32}$$
This is top-degree normalization, not a general finite-map trace. Algebraically its weight is justified by finite Artinian factorization: each length-one $S_q$ residue factor has $R$-length $f_q$, while normalization is generically the identity on every reduced component field. Smaller-dimensional factors have no degree-$n$ coefficient. In particular no inseparability is dropped and no vertical generic degree is fabricated. Every smaller-dimensional centre is still part of the function and conductor domain, with zero contribution in this convention.

For $E^1$ inputs, (32) proves that all top-dimensional pullbacks are $E^1$ and that this condition is equivalent to downstairs finite energy. Pass their bounded measures to the weak limits, a finite sum with fixed continuous restriction maps, to obtain
$$\mu_{E,R}(\boldsymbol u)=\sum_{\dim S_q=n}f_q\rho_{q,*}\mu_{E,S_q}(\rho_q^*\boldsymbol u).\tag{33}$$
G331 already proves full $D$ positivity descent: an upstairs tuple of $D$ functions descends exactly when constant on **every** restriction fibre, including conductor-infinite and nonminimal supports, all-zero, mixed-zero and partial-bottom cases. Combining this with (32) gives the exact energy descent statement: fibre-constant upstairs $D$ data descend to $E^1_R$ if and only if their top-dimensional entries have finite diagonal energy. No own lower-dimensional finite-energy condition is imposed; all lower-dimensional data still satisfy full fibre compatibility. At finite conductor value fibres are singletons; at infinite value equality on the conductor quotient is precisely the identification. Formula (33) adds masses on identified fibres. It asserts nothing about automatically tracing incompatible arbitrary upstairs tuples.

For every excellent reduced curve, B341's independent Cartier reference measure is
$$\mu_{\mathfrak a}=\sum_q f_q a_q\delta_{\operatorname{ord}_q/a_q},\qquad a_q=\operatorname{ord}_q(\mathfrak a)>0.$$
G331's actual $D$ is all extended nonpositive vectors on the finite branch set. Consequently $E^1$ is exactly the finite vectors, and
$$E(u)=\sum_q f_q a_q u(q),\qquad dE_u(v)=\sum_q f_q a_q v(q).\tag{34}$$
Every coefficient is strictly positive, so a single curve-branch pole has infinite energy. This is actual zero-arity Cartier energy on all primary curve models, with nonnormal and inseparable residue cases included, not an ideal-cone analogy. For example $R=k+t\ell[[t]]\subset\ell[[t]]$, $[\ell:k]=d$, has generic normalization degree one, residue degree $d$, and maximal-ideal reference mass $d$. Its primary ideal $t^r\ell[[t]]$ has multiplicity $dr$, so replacing the residue factor by a generic-degree-only factor is wrong, including for inseparable extensions. Gauge weights and profiles cancel exactly in (34). On a smooth DVR the maximal-ideal mass is one; a primary gauge $(t^r)$ has mass $r$ on its rescaled singleton. In dimension zero the reduction is a field, its centred section is empty, $E=0$ and the unique measure is zero. Nilpotents require the explicit reduction convention in n1: $k[[t]]$ and $k[[t]][\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ have the same reduced section and $(t)$ gauge but unreduced multiplicities one and two; no boundary-only reconstruction can distinguish those lengths.

notes.summary: Entire smooth finite-energy comparison with the canonical finite BFJ Definition4.3 local self-intersection convention, at exact published hypotheses.
notes.detailedSummary: A direct majorant proof compares all C majorants and nef Cartier majorants, giving the whole space and operator, not just bounded agreement. No unbounded energy theorem is inferred from the bounded grant; no forced Cegrell/global BJ identity or broadened multiplier scope.
notes.text:
Exact smooth specialization via the primary local intersection definition
Supports: G331, B341, n1, n4, n5, n6, n7.

The primary source is Boucksom--Favre--Jonsson, *Valuations and plurisubharmonic singularities*, published RIMS44 (2008), particularly its complete Setting, Proposition1.14, the relevant2.4--2.8 units, and **Definition4.3** within the entire Section4. The source has been read at its exact hypotheses: a smooth **closed** point of an affine variety over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, dimension $n\ge2$, with maximal-ideal section. No analytic arbitrary germ, positive characteristic, singular resolution, or broader multiplier theorem is asserted. G331 already supplies full cone comparison on all semivaluations with bottom adjoined; B341 supplies bounded operator comparison. These grants are not unbounded energy citations.

Here is an explicit local smooth extension convention, selected by a published **local** primary definition rather than a global projective energy theorem. For a BFJ formal psh function $g$, let $Z(g)$ be its nef Weil divisor. Define its local intersection energy and finite-energy class by
$$E_{\mathrm{BFJ,int}}(g)=\frac1n\langle Z(g)^{[n]}\rangle,\qquad E^1_{\mathrm{BFJ,int}}=\{g:\langle Z(g)^{[n]}\rangle> -\infty\},\tag{35}$$
where the bracket is **exactly BFJ Definition4.3**: the infimum of the intersections of nef Cartier majorants of its entries. The zero anchor, sign, raw multiplicity and degree-$n$ normalization are explicit; this is a local degree-$n$ energy, not a degree-$n+1$ projective Aubin--Mabuchi formula or a probability normalization. Equation (35) specifies the canonical finite-self-intersection convention; we do not claim the source uses this $E^1$ notation or proves an independently named energy theorem.

We prove the full comparison, rather than assume that convention agrees with truncation. Let $u_i\in D$ be nonbottom BFJ functions with associated $Z_i$. For a nef Cartier $W_i$, its function $w_i$ is continuous and belongs to $C$, by BFJ1.14 and G331's exact class comparison. Moreover $W_i\ge Z_i$ coefficientwise if and only if $w_i\ge u_i$ on the entire section. One direction is immediate at divisorial points. Conversely coefficient order gives function order there; on each closed simplex both formal functions are continuous by the precise G331/BFJ comparison, and rational divisorial points are dense, so order holds at every quasi-monomial. Taking their canonical infima over all retractions, as BFJ2.8 and G331 prescribe, preserves order at every semivaluation. B341's bounded operator comparison and the actual bounded test pairing of n4 identify $F(\boldsymbol w)=-\langle\boldsymbol W\rangle$.

Definition4.3's negative intersection is therefore the supremum over these Cartier majorants, which is at most the full $C$-majorant supremum (19). To prove the other bound, fix any $C$ majorants $h_i\ge u_i$. If one is zero, its form value is zero and contributes no positive supremum. Otherwise G331's normal zero dichotomy, or BFJ2.4 in this smooth range, gives $h_i\le-c_i<0$ uniformly. For $0<\eta<1$, approximate $(1-\eta)h_i$ uniformly by a rational primary profile $r_{i,\eta}$ with error less than $\eta c_i/2$ and tending to zero as $\eta\to0$. Then
$$r_{i,\eta}\ge h_i+\eta c_i/2\ge u_i.$$
Each is a nef Cartier majorant, and $r_{i,\eta}\to h_i$ uniformly. N4's uniform form convergence implies $F(\boldsymbol h)$ is at most the Cartier-majorant supremum. Thus
$$F_\infty(u_1,\ldots,u_n)=-\langle Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\rangle\quad\text{in }[0,\infty].\tag{36}$$
This argument does not invoke an unbounded continuity or energy grant from BFJ. It compares directly with its primary local definition. Zero target entries give zero on both sides; bottom has infinite self energy and is excluded from (35). G331 says every other $D$ function is a full BFJ function, so (36) proves equality of the **entire** finite-energy spaces under convention (35), not merely smooth core or bounded agreement.

For finite-energy tuples, Holder guarantees that the mixed moment with $Z(\mathfrak m)$ is finite. BFJ4.6's moment characterization at this mass condition and (22),(36) identify our finite-energy measure with its local intersection operator. Its integrability against every $E^1$ test is independently proved by (24), not inferred from an incomplete weak-test argument. Formula (21) shows uniqueness of the bounded decreasing extension under this convention: every individually bounded decreasing approximation of a specified finite-energy function gives the same energy and mixed operator. General primary gauges are transported by n7 with its one-factor law; no unpublished arbitrary-gauge theorem is attributed to BFJ. Smooth DVR and empty cases are n7.

This is a precise smooth local specialization, with published primary intersection definition and a proved canonical extension convention. It does **not** force equality with Cegrell classes of classical psh germs or with global projective BJ finite energy. Such spaces have different input objects and reference conventions. G331's geometric cone may contain the nodal vector $(-1,0)$; the qualified classical/CLD literal logarithmic radial obstruction remains unchanged. No literal radial comparison is claimed for the energy or measure.

Whole-original decision and evidence boundary

N2--n3 reconstruct the previously ungranted higher-dimensional geometric bridge and ordinary locality: Artinian-thickening Euler polynomials without coefficient fields, supported Koszul full symmetry, divisor-cycle projection preserving DVR degree, Rees diagonal/polarization, independently positive divisorial measures and their refinement lemma, the fixed primary correction and one common refinement giving actual invertible images, finite-span real-nef comparison, and the two compact-cover locality limits. N7 proves variable-cut gauge invariance with exactly one measure factor, residue-weighted normalization including inseparability, full conductor-fibre descent on all supports, nonpure zeros, actual curves and empty cases. No original P12.5 mathematical gap is retained **for this explicitly proved bounded-decreasing local intersection calculus**. Nonpluripolar Borel cutoff, quasicontinuity, Choquet capacity regularity and equation uniqueness are neither required to define this calculus nor proved here; they are not silently used. If a different smooth space or such stronger additional properties are required, they are separate comparison/theorem targets, not consequences of the present proof.
